name: Rijksmuseum
notes: The Dutch national museum; Rembrandt, Vermeer and the Golden Age collection. Book tickets well in advance.

name: Anne Frank House
notes: The hiding place where Anne Frank wrote her diary; deeply moving. Timed-entry tickets required, book weeks ahead.

name: Van Gogh Museum
notes: World's largest collection of Van Gogh's work. Pre-booking essential; sells out days in advance.

name: Vondelpark
notes: Amsterdam's most popular park; great for cycling, picnics and people-watching. Free open-air concerts in summer.

name: Grachtengordel – Canal Ring
notes: UNESCO-listed 17th-century canal ring; stroll or rent a bike along Prinsengracht and Keizersgracht.

name: Royal Palace Amsterdam
notes: 17th-century palace on Dam Square; opulent interiors with Golden Age art. Check ahead as it closes for royal events.

name: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
notes: Modern and contemporary art from Mondrian to Basquiat; the bathtub building is iconic.

name: Begijnhof
notes: Hidden medieval courtyard in the city centre; tranquil garden with one of Amsterdam's oldest wooden houses.

name: ARTIS Amsterdam Royal Zoo
notes: Europe's oldest zoo (1838); also has a planetarium and aquarium within the grounds.

name: Heineken Experience
notes: Interactive brewery tour in the original 1867 Heineken building; includes two beers in the price.

name: Café de Jaren
notes: Grand café on the Amstel with a large sunny terrace; great for reading, brunch or afternoon drinks.

name: Foodhallen
notes: Indoor food market in a former tram depot in Oud-West; 21 food stands from ramen to oysters.

name: Restaurant Moeders
notes: Beloved Dutch home-cooking spot in the Jordaan; walls plastered with customer photos of their mothers.

name: Pancakes Amsterdam
notes: Classic Dutch pancakes (thin, large, savoury and sweet) in the Nine Streets shopping area.

name: Albert Cuypmarkt
notes: The Netherlands' largest street market; cheap street food, stroopwafels, herring and fresh produce.

name: Café 't Smalle
notes: Classic 18th-century brown café in the Jordaan with a floating canal terrace; perfect for jenever tasting.

name: Worst Wijncafé
notes: Cosy natural wine bar with charcuterie boards; hidden-gem neighbourhood spot near Leidseplein.

name: Winkel 43
notes: Famous for arguably Amsterdam's best apple pie; right next to the Noordermarkt with a sunny terrace.

name: Drovers Dog
notes: Australian-style brunch café in Oud-West; excellent eggs, specialty coffee and fresh juices.

name: Bakers & Roasters
notes: Popular brunch spot in Kadijksplein; Brazilian-Kiwi fusion with great specialty coffee. Expect a queue on weekends.

name: Café Americain
notes: Art Nouveau grand café in the American Hotel on Leidsekade; stunning interior with stained glass.

name: Restaurant Rijks
notes: Michelin-starred restaurant inside the Rijksmuseum; modern Dutch cuisine with seasonal tasting menus.

name: Gebroeders Hartering
notes: Intimate wine-driven Dutch kitchen on Peperstraat; no fixed menu, just what's fresh. Reserve ahead.

name: Restaurant De Kas
notes: Farm-to-table dining inside a stunning 1926 greenhouse; ingredients grown on-site. Fixed daily menu.

name: Pllek
notes: Trendy container restaurant and bar on the IJ river in Noord; sandy beach terrace, good burgers and cocktails.

name: La Perla
notes: Beloved wood-fired Neapolitan pizza in the Jordaan; tiny, always busy, no reservations.

name: FEBO Automatiek
notes: Iconic Dutch fast-food automat; drop a coin, pull out a kroket or frikandel. A true Amsterdam experience.

name: Wil Graanstra Friteshuis
notes: Legendary frites stand at the Vondelpark entrance since 1956; get them with mayonnaise (patatje oorlog).

name: Restaurant Breda
notes: Modern European fine dining on Nes; tasting menus with a focus on fermentation and Dutch produce.

name: The Bulldog Coffeeshop
notes: Amsterdam's most famous coffeeshop chain; touristy but iconic, multiple locations near Leidseplein.

name: Grey Area
notes: Tiny American-run coffeeshop in the Jordaan; cult following for high-quality strains. Often a small queue outside.

name: Dampkring Coffeeshop
notes: Featured in Ocean's Twelve; cosy interior with good quality cannabis and a relaxed vibe.

name: Paradox Coffeeshop
notes: Mellow neighbourhood coffeeshop in the Jordaan; locals' favourite, also serves good sandwiches and fresh juice.

name: Boerejongens Coffeeshop
notes: Award-winning coffeeshop with multiple locations; known for top-shelf product and professional setup.

name: Noordermarkt
notes: Monday antiques market and Saturday organic farmers' market around the 17th-century Noorderkerk.

name: Free IJ Ferry to Amsterdam Noord
notes: Free public ferry from behind Centraal Station to Amsterdam Noord; great views of the IJ and easy access to NDSM and EYE.

name: Bloemenmarkt – Floating Flower Market
notes: World's only floating flower market on the Singel canal; tulip bulbs, Dutch souvenirs and fresh cut flowers.

name: EYE Filmmuseum
notes: Striking white building on the IJ riverbank in Noord; film screenings, exhibitions and great river-view café.

name: NEMO Science Museum
notes: Hands-on science museum in a ship-shaped green building; rooftop terrace with great harbour views (free entry).

name: Broodje Mokum
notes: Popular Amsterdam sandwich shop near Spui; try the classic uitsmijter or a fresh Dutch herring roll.

name: Schiphol Plaza Shopping
notes: Large shopping and dining centre connected to Schiphol arrivals hall; accessible without an air ticket.

name: Rijksmuseum Schiphol (Airport Gallery)
notes: Small but genuine Rijksmuseum gallery in Schiphol's departure lounge (post-security); free entry, real masterpieces.

name: Amsterdamse Bos
notes: Vast urban forest south of Amsterdam near Schiphol; cycling, rowing, goat farm and open-air theatre.

name: Cobra Museum of Modern Art
notes: Museum dedicated to the CoBrA art movement in Amstelveen; easy tram connection from Amsterdam or 10 min from Schiphol by taxi.

name: Keukenhof Gardens
notes: World-famous tulip garden open only March–May; 30 min from Schiphol by direct bus (Bus 858). Spectacular in spring.

name: Museum De Cruquius
notes: Historic steam pumping station that drained the Haarlemmermeer; fascinating Dutch water-management history.

name: McArthurGlen Designer Outlet Amsterdam
notes: Designer outlet mall a short walk from Schiphol; 100+ brands at discounted prices, accessible by shuttle or on foot.

name: Café-Restaurant De Rustende Jager
notes: Traditional Dutch brasserie in Badhoevedorp village, walkable from the Vienna House Easy hotel; hearty Dutch meals.

name: Restaurant Seinpost
notes: Good local restaurant in Hoofddorp town centre; 10 min taxi from Schiphol, solid Dutch-European menu.

name: Haarlem Grote Markt & St. Bavo Church
notes: Charming city just 15 min from Schiphol by train; beautiful Gothic church, great cafés and the Frans Hals Museum.

name: Royal FloraHolland Flower Auction Aalsmeer
notes: World's largest flower auction (building bigger than Monaco); visitor gallery open weekday mornings, 20 min from Schiphol.

name: Grand Café Brinkmann Hoofddorp
notes: Grand café on Hoofddorp's main square; Dutch standards, good beer selection, lively atmosphere on weekend evenings.

name: Ouderkerk aan de Amstel
notes: Picturesque village on the Amstel river south of Amsterdam; cycle there along the river, stop at a terrace café.

name: Molen De Zwaan – Badhoevedorp
notes: Working windmill in Badhoevedorp village, a 10-min walk from the Vienna House Easy hotel; open weekends.

name: Burgerlord – Schiphol Area
notes: Popular Dutch smash-burger chain in Schiphol Plaza; quick, good quality, much better than typical airport food.

name: Amsterdam Centraal Station
notes: Iconic 1889 neo-Gothic station; the main hub for trams, metro, trains and ferries. Grab a herring at a nearby stand.
